title: OpenTrust Dispute Resolution v1
description: Schema for dispute submissions to the Tier 3 human arbitration endpoint at https://registry.opentrust.dev/api/v1/disputes. Captures buyer and seller evidence, arbitrator decisions, and appeal status.

dispute_id.description: Unique dispute identifier (assigned by registry). Format: uuid or similar.

payment_tx_hash.description: Blockchain transaction hash or off-chain payment identifier for the disputed transaction.

escrow_amount_usdc.description: Amount in USDC held in escrow for this transaction.

buyer_identity.description: Verified identity of the buyer (from passport or verified blockchain address).

type.description: Identity type: GitHub OAuth, DID, or blockchain wallet address.

value.description: Identity value: GitHub username, DID string, or wallet address.

seller_tool_slug.description: Registry slug of the tool that was paid for (e.g., 'research-copilot', 'market-analyzer').

dispute_type.description: Category of dispute: non_delivery (Tier 2), partial_delivery (Tier 3), quality_dispute (Tier 3), or other.

submitted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when dispute was submitted by buyer.

buyer_evidence.description: Evidence and claim submitted by the buyer.

description.description: Buyer's description of the issue and why they believe delivery was insufficient.

request_timestamp.description: When the buyer made the payment request / initiated the transaction.

response_received.description: True if buyer received any response from the tool; false if no response or timeout.

http_status.description: HTTP status code of tool response, if any. Omit if no response received.

requested_remedy.description: What the buyer is asking for: full refund, partial refund, or re-delivery.

partial_refund_amount_usdc.description: If requested_remedy is 'partial_refund', the amount in USDC the buyer is requesting.

evidence_urls.description: URLs to logs, screenshots, recordings, or other evidence supporting the buyer's claim.

seller_evidence.description: Evidence and response submitted by the seller (tool author).

description.description: Seller's response: explanation of actions taken, delivery standard met, or technical rebuttal.

delivery_proof_url.description: URL to proof of delivery (e.g., signed attestation, delivery log, or output hash).

delivery_hash.description: Hash of delivered output (SHA-256 or declared hash type from proof_of_delivery config).

access_log_url.description: URL to tool's access or execution log showing buyer interaction and delivery timestamp.

arbitration_outcome.description: Decision issued by the assigned arbitrator (populated by registry after decision).

arbitrator_identity.description: GitHub handle or DID of the arbitrator who issued the decision.

decided_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when arbitrator issued the decision.

outcome.description: Arbitrator's decision: full refund to buyer, partial refund, seller wins, or appeal is pending.

refund_amount_usdc.description: Amount in USDC to be refunded to buyer (0 if seller wins).

rationale.description: Written explanation of the arbitrator's reasoning and interpretation of the delivery standard.

appeal_deadline.description: ISO 8601 deadline for either party to file an appeal. Null if appeal window has closed.

appeal_outcome.description: Decision issued by the appeal panel if the dispute was appealed (optional; populated only if appeal occurs).

appeal_filed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when appeal was filed.

appeal_rationale.description: Appealing party's reason for disputing the initial arbitrator's decision.

panel_arbitrators.description: GitHub handles or DIDs of the three arbitrators on the appeal panel.

panel_decided_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when appeal panel issued its final decision.

final_outcome.description: Panel's final decision (no further appeals allowed).

final_refund_amount_usdc.description: Final amount in USDC to be refunded to buyer after appeal.

panel_rationale.description: Written explanation of the panel's decision and any changes to the initial arbitrator's ruling.
